needs_you.ask: The sentences naming SLS staff (Sena and Caputo assaulting patients; Prichard calling the opt-out meeting) rest on an unsigned 2007 press release read through HEAL and a law-firm page now offline. Keep them?
choices: Keep the suit, drop the staff names until the complaint is read

research: Find the docket of Romano and Morgan v. SLS Residential, Inc. (S.D.N.Y., 2007; plaintiffs' counsel probably Michael Sussman) and read the complaint; replace the paraphrase of its claims (restraints, isolation rooms, nightly searches, patients' rights, ADA, $75M/$150M) with its own words (rule 31), and name who issued the Apr. 29, 2007 press release.

YourLawyer.com's SLS page (yourlawyer.com/new-york-medical-malpractice/sls-residential-defendants-sanctioned/) is a 404 as of Nov. 11, 2026: find a Wayback copy and archive it; it is the only source for the $35,000 sanction, the opt-out finding, Prichard's meeting and the sedation charge.
Find the year and outcome of Judge Robinson's $35,000 sanction ruling and of the class action itself.
Find the OMH charge that SLS sedated patients who refused medication in the court record (Matter of SLS Residential v. OMH, 2011) or other primary text.
Find when SLS stopped operating after the Nov. 2011 ruling.
Find a source naming the OMH commissioner who adopted the fines in July 2008 (Michael Hogan is not named by any cited source).
Check the clinical officer's spelling (Shawn Prichard vs Pritchard) against the court decisions.
Archive The Journal News, July 9, 2008 (lohud.com) original; it was read through HEAL's adult.htm reprint.
log: Nov 2: rebuilt on the Appellate Division decisions (Nov. 10, 2009; Nov. 15, 2011; Nov. 12, 2014), YourLawyer.com and Struggling Teens' LoHud roundup. Corrections: OMH filed revocation charges on Aug. 29, 2008 and revoked on Aug. 9, 2010 (not 2008); the Dec. 2008 ruling annulling the fines was reversed in 2009 and $100,000 reinstated ($10,000 restraint fine struck); 11 violations in all (8 + 3). Nov 3: restored the chairmen Joseph Santoro and Alfred Bergman, the affiliates and Route 6 headquarters (The Journal News, July 9, 2008, via HEAL's reprint), and the plaintiffs, named staff, the complaint's assault allegation and the $950-a-day price (Apr. 29, 2007 press release, print, via HEAL), all as allegations. Michael Hogan's name dropped (no source). Nov 11: no self-published survivor accounts in the record; the class action's claims stay as written because the YourLawyer page is now a 404 (research line above).
